abstract: Variations in the expression of histone genes influence the process of breaking dormancy in fission yeast spore cells. Since histones play a crucial role in chromatin organization, alterations in their expression impact chromatin states during spore germination, where such changes are vital. Although chromatin accessibility state has been studied in proliferating cells, there has been no specific research on spores. In this study, using ATAC-seq to examine chromatin accessibility in fission yeast spores, we found that ATAC-seq peaks frequently appeared as broad regions in gene-body in addition to promoter-linked narrow regions. Narrow peaks representing high chromatin accessibility at transcription start sites (TSSs) observed in proliferating cells were maintained in dormant spores as well as germinating spores, whereas broad peaks that cover gene-body were redistributed among different genes as germination progressed. The transition of broad open chromatin on gene-body was often linked with a stage-dependent transcriptional upregulation determined by scRNA-seq throughout dormancy breaking. Thus, the spore-specific chromatin alterations contribute to transcriptional changes observed during germination.
